key_insight: Outcome-only reinforcement learning can improve aggregate reward while degrading clinical decision procedures; dense credit for uncertainty-reducing questions improved diagnostic performance and robustness.
engineering_relevance: Train and evaluate multi-turn agents on how they gather information, not just final outcomes, to expose premature decisions and rare high-risk failures.
method: Build three controlled clinical environments: refill triage, diagnostic work-up, and dosing titration.
Use hidden clinical states, query costs, exact adaptive oracles, and deterministic outcome verifiers.
Compare outcome-only GRPO with dense process credit and separated exploration–exploitation training.
evidence_signal: Across three diagnostic training seeds, dense question credit improved held-out value and moderate-case support without the high-risk seed collapse observed under outcome-only training.
watch_item: Process-credit strength is task-dependent, and gains in high-risk support can come with excessive low-acuity questioning; controlled-environment results do not establish clinical readiness.
paper_title: Safe Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Clinical Agents: When Dense Rewards Beat Outcome Rewards
